Model the beam cross-section as a solid rectangle with width b equal to 50 mm and height h equal to 120 mm.
Assume linear-elastic, isotropic material behavior and small-deformation Euler-Bernoulli beam theory.
Set the origin of the vertical coordinate y at the centroidal neutral axis with positive y pointing vertically upward.
Apply a positive sagging bending moment M equal to 4000000 N mm acting about the horizontal centroidal principal axis.
Compute the second moment of area I about the horizontal centroidal axis using I equals b multiplied by h cubed divided by 12, yielding 7200000 mm^4.
Evaluate the bending normal stress distribution using the relation sigma equals negative M multiplied by y divided by I.
Determine the bending stress at the neutral axis y equals 0 mm, which evaluates to 0 MPa.
Determine the bending stress at the top fiber y equals 60 mm, which evaluates to negative 33.33 MPa in compression.
Determine the bending stress at the bottom fiber y equals negative 60 mm, which evaluates to positive 33.33 MPa in tension.
Report all stresses and geometric quantities using the N-mm-MPa unit system.
